exploit_name: Arbitrum retryable-ticket refund/value not verified enables timelock ETH exfiltration
description: GuardCM._verifySchedule() decodes the value parameter but never validates it. ProcessBridgedDataArbitrum.processBridgeData() validates only L2 target and payload selector, ignoring retryable-ticket parameters including excessFeeRefundAddress and callValueRefundAddress.
attack_scenario: Compromised Community Multisig schedules allowlisted L2 action with large timelock value and attacker-controlled refund addresses. Guard approves. On execution, Arbitrum refunds excess to attacker.
root_cause: GuardCM._verifySchedule() decodes the value parameter but never validates it. ProcessBridgedDataArbitrum.processBridgeData() validates only L2 target and payload selector, ignoring retryable-ticket parameters including excessFeeRefundAddress and callValueRefundAddress.
fix_description: Enforce value == 0 for bridged calls in GuardCM. Validate refund recipients and economic parameters in ProcessBridgedDataArbitrum.
notes: Loss of timelock ETH via unverified refund recipients, bypassing the guard's intended security boundary.
